name: language-root
body:
The language root of the code graph: one `Language` node per language actually scanned, derived ingestor-side from the `lang_switch` control record. It is the parent of every `Module` scanned under that language (`Language —Contains→ Module`) and the disjoint namespace that makes every module and symbol FQN language-rooted. Its FQN is the language id itself (`rust`, `go`, `java`, `cpp`, `ts`, `js`, `csharp`, `py`, `md`).

It is a real graph declaration, not a scanner fact: the frontends emit facts only and never a language record; the ingestor materialises one Language per stream it observes. Because every module FQN now begins with `<language-id>.`, the bare-id namespace is reserved for Language nodes and cannot collide with a module. Unaffected: `UnresolvedTarget` FQNs (foreign symbol names are not project identities and are not rooted) and `code_type` (path-based). Within-language collisions (a Java package sharing a type name) keep their existing shadowing/panic handling; cross-language collisions cannot occur because the roots are disjoint.

The language id that names this root is `domain.value.language-id`; the rooting behaviour it anchors is `domain.service.language-rooting`.
